title: Input-Dependent Power Usage in GPUs
problem: GPU power consumption during GEMM operations varies significantly based on input data characteristics (value distribution, bit similarity, placement, sparsity) while maintaining constant matrix shapes and sizes. This input-dependent power variation is not well understood and presents both challenges and optimization opportunities.
motivation: GPUs are major power consumers in AI-driven datacenters, making power optimization critical for energy efficiency and operational cost reduction.
method: The authors experimentally characterize GEMM power consumption by systematically varying input data across four dimensions: value distribution, bit similarity, placement, and sparsity, while keeping matrix shapes and sizes constant. They measure power variation across different data types and find up to 40% variation. They hypothesize this variation is caused by changes in bit flip rates in GPU hardware and propose leveraging this through compiler and scheduler optimizations.
key_novelty: Demonstrating that input-dependent data characteristics significantly affect GPU power consumption in GEMMs, enabling new power management optimization opportunities.
contributions: Experimental characterization showing up to 40% power variation in GPU GEMMs based solely on input data properties
Identification of four input variation dimensions affecting power: value distribution, bit similarity, placement, and sparsity
Hypothesis that bit flips in GPU hardware cause input-dependent power variations
Proposed compiler and scheduler optimizations for power management based on input characteristics
primary_theme: GPU power characterization and input-dependent optimization
